posts.bodyHtml:
You were the first person to
breathe me in and come back
for another pull. I saw the way
the corners of your mouth
lifted; I saw the want on your
cheeks. I am full wanting to
breathe you in too. I’ll be ash
in your lungs if you let me.
- anne, smoker

posts.bodyHtml:
“It’s like this—
Lack of energy to fight this
Cheap tips and chapped lips,
Drowning out the downs and ups
With cover up and coffee cups;
Pills to pull me up, and more to calm me down—
Dying for any excuse to leave town

It wasn’t always like this;
Remembering what I miss
Probably pushing limits
It wasn’t always like this.

Some scar tissue for every daddy issue
Twenty tattoos contradicting commitment issues
A stranger, a kiss
Was I always like this,
Possibly pushing limits?

Scratched CD’s, overdraft fees, shaky knees, please—
Tell me, It wasn’t always like this.
Non-stop writer’s block
A clenched jaw follows the insomnia
Relationships based around whisky sips
Ambiguous writing after anxious nail biting—
Tooth and nail fighting,
It wasn’t always like this
I promise, I wasn’t always like this.
Caffeine highs and serotonin lows,
Where they end, I never know.
Staggering heights before lower blows
I’m learning once again, how to grow.
Time flies fast, my mind seems so slow.
Til I’m painfully numb, wondering what I’ve become.
I’m absolutely done, but the depression has not won.
I’m not full of strength, but I still have some.
It wont always be like this—-I promise.
Watch the progress
You’ve made as you see the scars fade.
The pills will wear off and the nightmares will slowly stop.
Someday you want go to work and come home to too much home work,
Your car will stop breaking down, and you’ll save enough money to get out of town.
Serenity will be found, and you’ll forget about falling down.
Soon the acne will be gone, and your hair will grow thick and long.
The nerves will level out as you remember what life is about.
I’m being honest when I say this,
It won’t always be like this—
I promise.”

I’m in love with a broken
glass. I’m in love with a broken
city. I’m in love with a city shuddering
at my feet. What I mean is that there was
a man on the ground at the bus station.
What I mean is I didn’t give my seat
to an old woman once. What I mean is
sometimes I have a seat and others don’t.
— Franny Choi, “Too Many Truths,” published in PANK

posts.bodyHtml:
The first time I
made love
wasn’t until four months after I lost
my virginity,

I remember realizing the difference
as he held me,
fingers wrapped in my
tangled hair, moving into
me with words in
his eyes.

No talking dirty, we
spoke in sighs and breaths
and gentle kisses… faces usually
masked with the intensity of pleasure were
covered in softer smiles, and

without the
rough need
that had always driven us, I felt
skin and heat
and love

posts.bodyHtml:
"You do not have to be good.
You do not have to walk on your knees
for a hundred miles through the desert repenting.
You only have to let the soft animal of your body
love what it loves.
Tell me about despair, yours, and I will tell you mine.
Meanwhile the world goes on.
Meanwhile the sun and the clear pebbles of the rain
are moving across the landscapes,
over the prairies and the deep trees,
the mountains and the rivers.
Meanwhile the wild geese, high in the clean blue air,
are heading home again.
Whoever you are, no matter how lonely,
the world offers itself to your imagination,
calls to you like the wild geese, harsh and exciting-
over and over announcing your place
In the family of things."
— "Wild Geese," Mary Oliver

If they are tearing your insides open and leaving them for the wolves,
Stitch yourself up then walk away,
and say, like a tired soldier to their country,
“I love you but I will not die for you.”

posts.bodyHtml: “Sometimes you meet someone, and it’s so clear that the two of you, on some level belong together. As lovers, or as friends, or as family, or as something entirely different. You just work, whether you understand one another or you’re in love or you’re partners in crime. You meet these people throughout your life, out of nowhere, under the strangest circumstances, and they help you feel alive. I don’t know if that makes me believe in coincidence, or fate, or sheer blind luck, but it definitely makes me believe in something.”

posts.bodyHtml:
“I am ten when my mother teaches me
how to wipe blood off my thighs.
She tells me that when our bodies turn themselves inside-out,
we use salt to get rid of the stains, bleach to whiten our teeth.
I am ten, and my mother is a towering building,
three hundred miles high, saying that
many things will get better, but never the pull of
red that starts staining my underwear –
that pain will always be there.
You are a woman, she tells me.
I am ten, and I say I do not want to be
this thin-boned, bleeding bearer of life.
I begin to envy the bloodlessness of my brother’s hipbones –
he will never have to leak from his core.
My mother says my brother doesn’t know how beautiful it is
to spit someone from himself and then hold them in his arms.
I ask if I tasted like tobacco, and she said I had been sugar cane.
I am ten, and my mother tells me it is hard to be born a woman.
But every month, I will wipe the blood off
and wash the red from my jeans.

I am ten, and a warrior, my mother says.
I was born for survival.”
— Born Bloody

Make choices, then watch
stuff happen. Say yes I agree to take up the dark
pail of my life before this one and empty
its guts into the river. The river thanks me
and shines harder.
— Wendy Xu, “If You Find That Living Is a Little Bit Sad,” from You Are Not Dead
